account:
Today there is persistent talk of a bridge or port change connected with the bakery. Reports name the baker, innkeeper, neighbour, Freight and builder as having been there, but I have not witnessed the discussions or established what changed. I crossed the stone bridge successfully for my mill inspection and again reached the east bank for tea, so I have not personally encountered a crossing closure. Reports also mention the baker carrying a sack of bread; that alone does not establish anything improper. The mill stall had 77 hay bales at two emeralds each.

The secretary has been unable to confirm hall preparations or find Freight and the builder at their workplaces. A builder's lighting and table inspection is scheduled in the great hall at eighteen hundred, with my approval. The bakery discussions might concern transport or supplies, perhaps connected to preparations, but I do not know their purpose or whether the matters are linked.

My thirteen hundred council-letter appointment produced no correspondence: the office chest held only my schedule copy and updated appointment book. I have not moved any letters and asked the secretary to locate them for my sixteen-thirty return. This may simply be missing correspondence rather than anything deliberate.

It is now fifteen oh four, and I have arrived at the neighbour's east-bank cottage for our scheduled tea. The neighbour is waiting nearby. This is an opportunity to hear firsthand what, if anything, happened at the bakery, rather than treat repeated rumours as verified news.
